title: A naked mole-rat can survive 18 minutes with no oxygen at all
body: Naked mole-rats live in crowded, poorly ventilated burrows in East Africa, where oxygen runs low and carbon dioxide runs high. In a zero-oxygen atmosphere they survive 18 minutes apparently unharmed, and in air with only 5% oxygen, about a quarter of normal, they last at least five hours. Their trick is to **switch fuel**: when oxygen is gone, their cells break down fructose instead of glucose through a pathway that needs no oxygen, producing lactic acid. How they tolerate the resulting acid build-up without tissue damage was still unknown as of 2017.

slides.label: survived in a zero-oxygen atmosphere, apparently without harm
slides.text: At 5% oxygen, about a quarter of what normal air holds, a naked mole-rat lasts at least five hours.

slides.heading: How long a naked mole-rat lasts at each oxygen level
slides.note: Dry air at sea level is 20.95% oxygen

slides.heading: Running on fructose
slides.text: Most mammal cells rely on glucose, and the main way of burning it stalls without oxygen. The naked mole-rat instead feeds fructose into anaerobic glycolysis, a pathway that works with no oxygen at all, and makes lactic acid as the by-product.

slides.heading: More mole-rat oddities
items: The first mammal found to be eusocial: one queen breeds, with one to three males
Feels no pain from acid or from capsaicin, the heat of chillies
Lives more than 30 years, longer than any other rodent
Nearly cold-blooded: its body temperature tracks the burrow

slides.question: Which fuel keeps a naked mole-rat going when the oxygen runs out?
slides.explanation: With no oxygen, its cells push fructose through anaerobic glycolysis, a pathway that needs no oxygen, producing lactic acid.
